question: Two patients present with toxin-mediated SNARE proteins. One has generalized muscle rigidity, the other has flaccid paralysis after eating canned food. What is the mechanism of action of these toxins:

options.B: Inhibition of neurotransmitter release at the presynaptic membrane

explanation:
Botelium Toxin: Affects peripheral cholinergic nerve terminals. By cleaving SNARE proteins (like SNAP-25, syntaxin or synaptobrevin) it prevents the release of acetylcholine which causes flaccid paralysis.
Tetanus Toxin: It travels retrogradely to the central nervous system and targets inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells) in the spinal cord. By destroying SNARE proteins there it blocks the release of inhibitory neurotransmitters (GABA and glycine) resulting in unopposed muscle overstimulation and spastic paralysis or rigidity.
